headline: Every major sits below its 200-day line, yet Bitcoin's momentum and ETF tape are quietly firming
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles the argument before anyone opens their mouth about RSI. All seven majors, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, ADA, sit below their 200-day moving averages. No golden crosses anywhere on the board. That is not a mixed market, that is a market still working through a broad drawdown: BTC is 48.1% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is down 60.2% from its own peak, and ADA is off a brutal 81.3%. When every asset agrees on the same side of the trend line, the story is the trend, not the ticker.

But trend and momentum are not telling identical stories right now, and that gap is worth naming. BTC's RSI-14 sits at 55.6 with MACD above signal, both readable as a market resting comfortably mid-range rather than oversold or overheated. ETH's RSI is even higher at 57.6, yet its MACD sits below signal, a small divergence: price and momentum indicators disagreeing on direction even as the number looks constructive. XRP is the outlier on the soft side, RSI at 37.6, MACD below signal, chg_7d at -3.6%, the only asset showing real weakness across both timeframes. So under a uniformly bearish 200-day picture, short-term momentum is quietly split between resting and fading, not falling apart.

Positioning adds texture rather than alarm. BTC funding on OKX is 0.0056% per 8 hours (6.1% annualized), modestly positive but nowhere near frothy, with open interest at $2.09B and a long/short ratio of 1.39. Liquidations over the past 23 hours ran $4.25M short-side versus $553K long-side, meaning shorts got squeezed more than longs, consistent with a market grinding sideways-to-up against a crowd leaning bearish. DOGE stands out for crowded optimism: funding at 10.7% annualized and a long/short ratio of 5.29, the kind of lopsided book that gets fragile if price stops cooperating. XRP's long/short ratio of 3.72 against negative RSI momentum is a similar tension, a crowd betting long into a chart that isn't confirming it.

Flows are where the disagreement with sentiment gets interesting. Whale wallets moved a net $29.0 million off exchanges in the past 48 hours, BTC specifically showing $176.99M in outflows against $147.97M in inflows, coins leaving venues rather than piling up for sale. Zoom out to the weekly trend and the picture is choppier: the last four weekly readings ran +$1.005B, +$1.117B, then two negative prints of -$589M and -$296M, so the current 48-hour outflow sits inside a series that recently flipped negative before this latest positive tick. On the ETF side, BTC funds took in $38.7M on 18 Aug, part of an $87.8M net over the last five sessions with only 2 same-direction days, so call it a positive but not yet a settled run. ETH ETFs added $5.6M on the same day, $49.8M over five sessions. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, actually shrank 0.58% over 30 days to $306.5B, a mild fade rather than a build-up of sideline cash.

Layer sentiment on last, because it's the foil here. Fear & Greed reads 41, still labeled Fear and sitting at the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 41. The crowd is cautious, prices are below long-term trend across the board, yet BTC's short-term momentum is neutral-to-firm, its ETF flows are net positive over five sessions, and whale wallets just pulled coin off exchanges rather than staging it for sale. That's a crowd feeling worse than the tape in front of them is currently behaving. Worth watching from here: whether BTC's ETF flow turns into more than 2 same-direction days, whether the weekly whale net flips back decisively positive after two down weeks, and whether DOGE's and XRP's crowded long positioning gets tested against their weaker RSI readings.
